findings.problem: The “Find the biggest!” wish tag is dimmed to 0.55 opacity from 2.2 s and stays that way for the rest of the scene (about 7 s). Its text then measures about 2.2:1 against white (darkest pixel rgb 173,173,173). That is below the 4.5:1 the brand guarantees for text on light, which is what the --text-dim / -ink shades are for. Opacity is the only thing breaking it.
findings.fix: Keep the wish at full opacity so the c-grey ink (--text-dim, 5.3:1) is used as designed, and show that it has been superseded another way: fade it out entirely once the first tick lands, or change it to the dashed grey outline with no text. Do not use an opacity below about 0.8 on any text that stays on screen.
findings.evidence: Measured on node tools/video-still.js algo-1 s2@7.5 (abs 11.5 s). A scan of all text opacities every 0.3 s found this is the only sustained low-opacity text in the video: 25 frames at opacity 0.55 to 0.67, local 0.4 to 9.4 s. Source: wish.set({... o: clamp(wk * 4) * (1 - 0.45 * ramp(t, 2.2, 2.6, E.lin))}) in scene-02-recipe.js.

findings.problem: In the reveal, the “via teleport” pill is drawn on top of the X visit-share bar. It covers the right end of the track and sits right next to the “5%” figure, so the X bar and its green exact-share marker look crowded and partly hidden at the moment the scene makes its point about the teleport floor.
findings.fix: Move the pill off the bar. Put it in the empty space under the X row, between that row and the hops card (about 20 px of clearance), or to the right of the 5% label. Keep it purple soft. Do not let it overlap any track or marker.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-1 s8@11.7 (abs 84.7 s), and the zoom of that still: the pill spans the X track from just right of the marker to the 5% label.

findings.problem: The “n = 16 → double n” row sits 2 px above the top of the stage (tag box top at stage y -2) and only about 25 px under the second headline line. The rule is everything inside the stage with at least a 12 px margin. It also reads as crowded against the headline. The bottom of the stage has roughly 40 px spare.
findings.fix: Move the whole figure (the n tag row, the three column heads and everything under them) down by about 14 px, or shrink the vertical gaps by a few px, so the n tag starts at least 12 px inside the stage.
findings.evidence: DOM audit at abs 41 s (s5 local 3.0): v-tag solid c-blue spans L275 T-2 R445 B62 in stage coordinates. node tools/video-still.js algo-1 s5@3.0 shows the tag close under “watch the work”.

findings.problem: The halving-loop “÷2” tags use a typed ÷ glyph, while the “×2” and “+1” signature tags in the same scene draw their operator as an SVG icon. It is inconsistent inside one scene, and the brand rule prefers symbols drawn as SVG.
findings.fix: Draw a small divide icon (a bar with two dots) beside the digit 2 in the ÷2 tags, using the same icon helper and size ratio as the × and + icons. Or add one comment saying small tags deliberately keep the glyph.
findings.evidence: scene-05-doubling.js line 151: A1.tag(stage, { text: "÷2", ... }). Visible in node tools/video-still.js algo-1 s5@9.0 next to the drawn “× 2” and “+ 1” tags.

findings.problem: The three step chips read “1 links”, “2 repair” and “3 teleport”. “1 links” looks like a plural error, and the numeral could be read as a count of links rather than a step number.
findings.fix: Write them as “links”, “repair” and “teleport” with a small numbered circle drawn beside each. Or use “step 1: links”. Keep the chip widths (w: 150 / 170 / 190), which already fit.
findings.evidence: node tools/video-still.js algo-1 s9@3.25, s9@6.5 and s9@9.75 (abs 88.25, 91.5 and 94.75 s). Source: CHIPS in scene-09-matrix.js lines 55-59.
